summary: The visual-qa-engineer stage reports itself UNCONFIGURED for the reagent map because no Playwright screenshot baselines exist for it. This feature adds `@visual`-tagged `toHaveScreenshot()` tests for the map's stable DOM chrome (site list, page header/nav link, and a new error-state element) and one tolerant test of the Cesium canvas at its fixed default view, storing baselines per runner image (debian/ubi9) via a `RUNNER_VARIANT`-keyed `snapshotPathTemplate`. `scripts/ui-suite-in-chrome.sh` gains an `--update-baselines` flag to regenerate them explicitly; the tests skip on a developer Mac (no `RUNNER_VARIANT`) and never skip in the runner image. `ReagentMapView.vue` currently has no visible error-state element, so one must be added for the error-state screenshot to mean anything, without weakening the existing resilience test's assertions. Docs close the 'No visual baselines' known gap and describe when to regenerate baselines, including after a browser-lock bump.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: `apps/ye-olde-magic-shop/tests/reagent-map-visual.spec.ts` MUST hold `@visual`-tagged `toHaveScreenshot()` tests for the site list, the page header with its nav link, and the view's error state when `/api/reagent-sites` fails through route interception.
examples: page.route('**/api/reagent-sites', route => route.abort('failed')) — same pattern as reagent-map-resilience.spec.ts's REAGENT_SITES_API_PATTERN

acceptanceCriteria.statement: One `@visual` test MUST cover `#cesiumContainer` at the fixed default view, after `cesium.waitForSettled()`, with a stated `maxDiffPixelRatio` that never exceeds 1%.

If the globe `@visual` test is flaky under the five-run repeat criterion, the developer MUST remove it, mask the canvas in the other `@visual` tests, and record why in the delivery record, instead of raising the tolerance past 1%.

`playwright.config.ts` MUST store baselines per runner image under `.playwright-baselines/{debian,ubi9}/` using `snapshotPathTemplate`, keyed by a `RUNNER_VARIANT` environment variable that `scripts/ui-suite-in-chrome.sh` sets.
examples: snapshotPathTemplate: '.playwright-baselines/{arg}{ext}' where {arg} is built from resolveRunnerVariant() + the test's own snapshot name, mirroring resolveRunnerSlowMo()/resolveRunnerVideo()'s read-env-at-call-time pattern

acceptanceCriteria.statement: When `RUNNER_VARIANT` is unset, as on a developer's Mac, every `@visual` test MUST skip with a message stating why. When it is set, the tests MUST never skip, and a missing baseline MUST fail the test.

`scripts/ui-suite-in-chrome.sh --update-baselines`, alone or combined with `--ubi9`, MUST regenerate that image's baselines by passing `--update-snapshots` to Playwright. Without the flag, the script MUST never write a baseline. `ui-suite-in-chrome.test.sh` MUST cover the flag.
The suite MUST pass five consecutive runs in each image (debian and ubi9), and the run output MUST be recorded in the delivery record.

A one-line style change to the site list MUST fail the matching `@visual` test in both images. A moved default camera on the globe test, if that test stays, MUST do the same. The failing output MUST be recorded, then the change reverted.

`docs/testing-cesium.md` and `docs/runner-image.md` MUST document how and when to regenerate baselines, including after a browser lock bump. `testing-cesium.md`'s 'No visual baselines' Known Gaps entry MUST be closed. Both documents MUST follow `.claude/rules/writing-style.md`.

Every new or changed function MUST have cyclomatic complexity below 7. Every changed line MUST be covered by a test that can fail. No file outside `scope.paths` MUST change, except this run's own delivery record under `docs/features/reagent-map-visual-baselines/`.

`ReagentMapView.vue` MUST render a visible, stable error-state element when `fetchReagentSites()` rejects, since none exists today and the error-state screenshot in the first acceptance criterion needs something stable to capture.
examples: A `data-testid="reagent-map-error"` element with `role="alert"`, set via a new ref just before the existing `throw sitesResult.reason`, so the existing pageerror event, `newViewer.destroy()` call, and the zero-canvas/zero-list-item assertions in `reagent-map-resilience.spec.ts` stay intact.

nonFunctionalRequirements.requirement: The suite MUST keep running with `--workers=3`, `--shm-size=1g`, and the existing app-health timeout; adding visual baselines MUST NOT change any of these.
The new error-state element MUST be exposed to assistive technology consistently with the existing `role`/`aria-label` pattern already used on `#cesiumContainer` and the site list.
Baseline PNGs MUST be generated and compared only inside the Saturday runner image (debian or ubi9), never on a developer's Mac, since the same page renders differently on each.

proposedFitnessFunctions.verification: Playwright toHaveScreenshot() under --project=chrome, run via scripts/ui-suite-in-chrome.sh

proposedFitnessFunctions.verification: ui-suite-in-chrome.test.sh asserts --update-snapshots is passed to playwright only when --update-baselines is given

proposedFitnessFunctions.property: Cyclomatic complexity below 7 on every changed function
Globe canvas screenshot stability across 5 repeated runs per image
proposedFitnessFunctions.verification: Manually recorded five-run pass in the delivery record per image; a one-time stability proof, not a per-commit CI gate

architecturalFlags: ReagentMapView.vue has no visible error-state element today — onMounted rethrows on a fetchReagentSites() rejection with no rendered feedback. The error-state acceptance criterion requires an @visual screenshot of 'the error state,' which needs a stable, visible element to exist first. Adding one is additive UI markup, not a change to the Cesium view's camera or behavior, so it stays inside the spirit of the 'Changing the view itself' out-of-scope item — flagging for human confirmation since the literal wording could be read either way.

Skipping architect: this feature is additive within the existing Saturday/Playwright visual-testing pattern (toHaveScreenshot, @visual tag, snapshotPathTemplate) and the existing per-image runner pattern (RUNNER_VARIANT mirrors RUNNER_SLOW_MO/RUNNER_VIDEO already read at call time in playwright.config.ts). No new package, base class, or layer boundary is introduced.

Skipping security-reviewer: Trust Boundaries states no auth, no user input, no external calls; the only trust-boundary-shaped code is the existing route-interception test pattern reused from reagent-map-resilience.spec.ts, already reviewed under reagent-map-globe.

developer: Add a visible, stable error-state element to ReagentMapView.vue (data-testid="reagent-map-error", role="alert"), set via a new ref just before the existing `throw sitesResult.reason`, preserving the existing pageerror event, newViewer.destroy() call, and the zero-canvas/zero-list-item assertions in reagent-map-resilience.spec.ts.

Create apps/ye-olde-magic-shop/tests/reagent-map-visual.spec.ts with @visual-tagged toHaveScreenshot() tests: page header + nav link, site list, the new error-state element (via the same route-interception pattern as reagent-map-resilience.spec.ts), and #cesiumContainer at the default view after cesium.waitForSettled() with an explicit maxDiffPixelRatio <= 0.01.
Gate every @visual test on process.env.RUNNER_VARIANT: skip with a stated reason when unset, never skip (missing baseline fails) when set.

Add snapshotPathTemplate to playwright.config.ts storing baselines under .playwright-baselines/{debian,ubi9}/, reading RUNNER_VARIANT at call time the same way resolveRunnerSlowMo()/resolveRunnerVideo() already do.

Add --update-baselines to scripts/ui-suite-in-chrome.sh (composable with --ubi9): export RUNNER_VARIANT into the container in start_container(), and pass --update-snapshots to the chrome suite run only when the flag is set; never write a baseline otherwise.

Extend scripts/ui-suite-in-chrome.test.sh to cover --update-baselines alone and combined with --ubi9, asserting the docker exec log contains --update-snapshots only when the flag is passed and RUNNER_VARIANT is exported in both variants.
Run scripts/ui-suite-in-chrome.sh --update-baselines and --ubi9 --update-baselines once each to generate and commit the initial baselines under .playwright-baselines/{debian,ubi9}/.
Run the suite five consecutive times in each image and record the output for the delivery record.
Make and revert a one-line site-list style change (and, if the globe test stays, a moved default camera) in each image, recording the failing output for the delivery record.

Verify a missing baseline fails (not skips) when RUNNER_VARIANT is set, using a disposable run with a baseline file temporarily renamed.

edgeCases.case: RUNNER_VARIANT is set to a value other than 'debian' or 'ubi9'.
edgeCases.handling: Treat as an unrecognized variant and fail loudly rather than silently falling back to one baseline directory, since a silent fallback would compare against the wrong image's baselines.

edgeCases.case: The globe @visual test is flaky across the five-run check.
edgeCases.handling: Remove it, mask the canvas region in the other @visual tests, and record why — per the acceptance criterion's own fallback, not a tolerance increase past 1%.

edgeCases.case: A baseline file is missing in the runner image (RUNNER_VARIANT set).
edgeCases.handling: The test MUST fail, never skip — skipping is reserved for RUNNER_VARIANT being unset entirely.

edgeCases.case: Both buildViewer() and fetchReagentSites() reject at once.
edgeCases.handling: Existing onMounted logic already rethrows viewerResult's rejection first and never reaches the sitesResult branch; the new error-state element only renders on a sitesResult rejection after buildViewer() succeeds, matching the resilience spec's covered branch and the error-state acceptance criterion's literal scope (/api/reagent-sites failing).

definitionOfDone: reagent-map-visual.spec.ts exists with @visual-tagged toHaveScreenshot() tests for the site list, the header/nav link, the error state, and (if kept) the globe default view.
playwright.config.ts's snapshotPathTemplate stores baselines under .playwright-baselines/{debian,ubi9}/, keyed by RUNNER_VARIANT.
@visual tests skip with a stated reason when RUNNER_VARIANT is unset, and never skip (missing baseline fails) when it is set.
scripts/ui-suite-in-chrome.sh supports --update-baselines (alone and with --ubi9), writing a baseline only when passed; ui-suite-in-chrome.test.sh covers it.
Both debian and ubi9 images pass five consecutive runs; the output is recorded in the delivery record.
A one-line site-list style change, and a moved default camera if the globe test stays, each fail their matching @visual test in both images; the failing output is recorded and the change reverted.
docs/testing-cesium.md's 'No visual baselines' Known Gaps entry is closed, and docs/runner-image.md documents regenerating baselines after a browser lock bump; both pass writing-style review.
Every new or changed function has cyclomatic complexity below 7; every changed line is covered by a test that can fail; no file outside scope.paths changes except this run's own delivery record.
visual-qa-engineer, run after this merges, finds .playwright-baselines/ and stops reporting UNCONFIGURED for this feature.
openQuestions: The spec's own open question is carried forward as an assumption: regenerate baselines in the same PR as any browser-lock bump, which docs/runner-image.md will state.

Human confirmation requested: adding a visible error-state element to ReagentMapView.vue (none exists today) is needed to make the error-state acceptance criterion's screenshot meaningful. This is additive markup, not a change to the Cesium view's camera or behavior — flagging since 'Changing the view itself' is listed as out of scope and the wording could be read either way.

Whether the globe @visual test (#cesiumContainer) survives the five-run flakiness check is unresolved until the developer actually runs it in both images; the acceptance criteria already specify the fallback (remove it, mask the canvas, record why) if it doesn't.

No retrospective.md or delivery-summary.md 'What to Improve' section exists yet for any prior feature in this repo to mine for cross-cutting process lessons; the applicable same-bounded-context precedent is reagent-map-globe's visual-qa-engineer.md, whose canvas-is-a-poor-pixel-diff-target recommendation is already folded into the globe test's flakiness fallback.
